description: Security misconfigurations or weaknesses detected on web-facing services.
Email authentication and security configuration issues (SPF, DKIM, DMARC).
Exposed or misconfigured network services and open ports.
IP addresses or domains associated with malicious activity or poor reputation.
Risks relating to brand impersonation, typosquatting, or reputational threats.
Exposed assets or services that increase the organisation's attack surface.
DNS configuration issues including expired domains, missing records, and zone transfer risks.
Known CVE-based software vulnerabilities detected on monitored assets.
Exposed sensitive data or data leakage risks detected on public-facing systems.
TLS/SSL configuration weaknesses, expired certificates, or missing HTTPS enforcement.
Risks identified through vendor security questionnaire responses.
Verified security vulnerabilities detected via automated scanning.
Registered domain permutations that may be used for phishing or brand abuse.
Exposed email addresses or credentials identified in data breach monitoring.
Sensitive data found exposed on public sources or dark web monitoring.
Risks identified from manually uploaded evidence documents.
A condition in a software, hardware, or service component that could contribute to the introduction of vulnerabilities. E.g., a CWE.
